name: Interdisciplinary Studies in Agriculture & Life Sciences (BS)

rows.label: You cannot be admitted to this major on entering CALS or by internal transfer; you move into it later, after your interests diverge from your current major
Apply to the major through the Major Application form, with your goals and course plan
Have an academic advisor agree to guide your proposed program
This major cannot be combined with a second major (minors are fine)
One oral communication course (ORL-AG, or advisor-approved)
rows.note: Only ORL-AG courses are recognised here; a course your advisor approves instead must be confirmed with them.

rows.label: If your advisor approved a different oral communication course in place of an ORL-AG one, confirm that approval
rows.note: The planner only recognises ORL-AG courses above; an advisor-approved substitute cannot be seen here.

rows.label: One calculus or statistics course
rows.note: The page names no specific courses, so the planner cannot check this; confirm with your advisor.

rows.label: Three lower-level courses (1100-2999) in your own focus area
rows.note: The focus area is set with your advisor, so the planner cannot check it. Plan these with your advisor.

rows.label: Five or more upper-level courses (3000 and up) in your own focus area
rows.note: The focus area is set with your advisor, so the planner cannot check it. Plan these with your advisor.

rows.label: At most 6 credits of Information Science (INFO) courses count toward focus-area courses
Focus-area courses form a coherent plan approved with your advisor
rows.note: Courses should span disciplines and move from introductory to advanced; unstructured coursework limits and sub-3-credit courses need advisor sign-off.

rows.label: At least 10 courses in total across the major requirements
rows.note: Roughly 30 credits for most students, but the total varies with your course choices.
